EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  September 25, 2017

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Susan Brtis
Carol Dean-Porter
Patricia Harik
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST 28, 2017
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ noted that MEMBER PERSICHINA was present at this meeting and
that the draft Minutes of August 28, 2017 should be amended.

MEMBER DEAN-PORTER moved, seconded by MEMBER HARIK

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE AUGUST 28, 2017 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS AMENDED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None.

PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT TEMPORARY HORSE BOARDING
LOGISTICS
The Community Services Director reported that a meeting had been recently held at the Peter
Weber Equestrian Center with PWEC Concession Operator Gill Houle, Nancy Wildman,
Angie Gilbride, and two residents who will need their horses re-located during the California
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 25, 2017  1
 Water Company project. He noted that the Palos Verdes Landfill staff have approved the
proposed temporary installation of pipe corrals on a former equestrian center renovation
project staging site adjacent to the Equestrian Center. Gil Houle indicated that he was
obtaining bids and working with Angie Gilbride, Regional Community Affairs Specialist for
California Water Service Company, for the proposed installation of fully covered, 12’ x 24’
pipe corrals with rubber mats.

In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’S inquiries, Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, stated that
of the approximately 20 horses being boarded in private residence stables along the trail
section were within the Water Reliability Project’s scope of work and that approximately 12
horses would need to be relocated to the proposed temporary pipe corrals site. She also
reported that all of the owners of the 12 horses are agreeable to the proposed relocation.

Angie Gilbride responded to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’S inquiry that the work in this trail section
would probably last four to five months and begin in approximately one year. MEMBER
BRTIS stated that the proposed installation of pipe corrals next to the Peter Weber Equestrian
Center would be a good alternative for the relocated horses, as Gil Houle’s staff provides
excellent horse boarding services.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ reported that California Water Company had provided City Council
with an Arborist Report on the trail trees that may be impacted during the project. Angie
Gilbride stated that it was California Water Company’s goal to remove or impact as few City
trail trees as possible during the project. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ thanked Nancy Wildman for
volunteering to coordinate the relocation of horses in her neighborhood and Angie Gilbride for
keeping the Equestrian Committee up to date on the progress of the project.

EQUESTRIAN IMPROVEMENTS AND ACTIVITIES REPORT
The Community Services Director highlighted the first annual report’s information and
encouraged the Equestrian Committee to provide any feedback to improve the report.
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ stated that it was very important that the City document the level of
financial and programming support that the City provides annually to the equestrian
community.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

BOTANICAL GARDENS TRAIL CROSSING MEASURES
The Community Services Director reviewed the trail crossing safety measures that were
implemented by the Equestrian Committee four years ago to allow shared parking between
the South Coast Botanic Gardens, Rolling Hill Country Day School, and Rolling Hills United
Methodist Church for large special events and meetings. He then reviewed the steps and
costs incurred by the City and the three entities in order to abide by the safety measures,
noting that there had never been a safety incident during this four-year period.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 25, 2017  2
 In response to MEMBER SHINN’S inquiry, Tanya Finney, South Coast Botanic Gardens
Superintendent, indicated that trail monitoring staff costs were incurred by each entity holding
a special event or meeting and also by the Botanic Gardens for their staff to lock the gate
after every event. MEMBER SHINN stated that she would not be in favor of changing the
current trail crossing safety measures.

MEMBER SILVANO concurred with MEMBER SHINN noting that the people crossing the trail
were not equestrians and without a trail crossing safety monitor in place a major incident
could occur. Several COMMITTEE MEMBERS indicated they were also not in favor of
revising or reducing the current safety measures.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER DEAN-PORTER

  TO MAINTAIN THE CURRENT TRAIL CROSSING SAFETY MEASURES FOR
  PARKING LOT SHARING EVENTS AND MEETINGS HELD BY THE SOUTH COAST
  BOTANIC GARDENS, ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY DAY SCHOOL, AND ROLLING
  HILLS UNITED METHODIST CHURCH.

AYES: Brtis, Dean-Porter, Harik, Persichina, Schmitz, Shinn, and Silvano

DAPPLEGRAY PARK DRESSAGE ARENA ISSUE
The Community Services Director reported that he was asked by a Horse Trainer to have the
Equestrian Committee consider the issue of riders bringing small barrels into the Dapplegray
Park junior dressage arena to practice barrel racing. The parents of a youth rider also
contacted the City to verify whether there was an arena rule prohibiting this activity. The
parents also noted that their daughter always took the arena rake and groomed the footing
where needed when she was done. The Community Services Director stated that if a new
arena rule was to be implemented by the Equestrian Committee, that it would likely be
applicable to all the City’s public arenas.

MEMBER DEAN-PORTER stated that the public arenas should be inclusive of all riding styles
and was not in favor of restricting this activity in any of the City’s public arenas. Other
COMMITTEE MEMBERS concurred.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

CHANDLER PARK ARENA RULES
The Community Services Director reported that Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, had
requested that this item be placed on the Equestrian Committee agenda. He indicated that
she regularly observes Horse Trainers violating the arena’s rules. In response to Ms.
Schachter’s inquiry, the Community Services Director stated that the City’s Administrative
Services Director was obtaining additional park security camera project quotes, since the
initial quote was significantly higher than expected. He also reported that two new City
Crossing Guards for Rancho Vista School (AM and PM shifts) were being hired and would
also assist City staff member, Jessica Slawson, with part-time code enforcement duties.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 25, 2017  3
 CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ requested that an update on the progress of installing park security
cameras be placed on the Committee’s Future Agenda Items list, and that until the cameras
are installed, the new part-time Crossing Guards will be assigned to periodically monitor
Chandler Park arena. In response to the Community Services Director’s inquiry, Ms.
Schachter indicated that the peak training times in Chandler arena during the weekdays were
from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. and on weekends from 8:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ noted that other than the Chandler Park arena rules violation report,
the other items listed were routine.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  Audience member, Pam Schachter, requested that signs be posted with the date and
  time period notifying Chandler Park arena riders that tree stumps will be ground out
  near the arena. Member Shinn requested signs be posted on the rear fence and
  preceding 4 Goldring Place to forewarn trail riders of rear yard construction taking
  place. In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’S inquiry, the Community Services
  Director stated that a Portuguese Bend National Horse Show volunteer will install two
  bay windows on the new Horse Show Judges Booth at no cost to the City.

B.  EQUESTRIAN/PEDESTRIAN STREET CROSSINGS PROJECT UPDATE
  The Community Services Director reported that while there has not been any recent
  work done, the project is still expected to be completed in October as planned.
  CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked that MEMBER KEMP (absent) be updated.

C.  CITY CELEBRATION EVENT
  The Community Services Director thanked MEMBERS SHINN, SILVANO, HARIK, and
  audience members Pam Schachter and Nancy Wildman for coordinating the
  horsemanship events at this year’s City Celebration. He also requested that comments
  and suggestions for this year’s Debriefing Report be submitted to him by October 15 th.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PARK SECURITY CAMERAS UPDATE

B.  CHANDLER PARK ARENA FOOTING PROJECT UPDATE

C.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 25, 2017  4
 ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER DEAN-PORTER moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 7:42 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
